Senators concerned about nuclear proliferation have secured a vote on the agreement before the end of Congress’ 90-day review period, Reuters reported Friday. Trump submitted the pact, known as a 123 Agreement, to Congress in late August. It entered the Senate record on Sept. 14, starting the 90-day review period during which lawmakers can seek to pass a resolution of disapproval.

(D-Ore.) said the Senate will have an opportunity to examine the agreement’s potential impact on nuclear proliferation and the risk of a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. He said he worked with Republicans to secure the vote, alongside fellow Democratic senators Sen.

Democratic lawmakers and nuclear nonproliferation advocates have criticized the agreement because they say it does not bar Saudi Arabia from enriching uranium or reprocessing nuclear waste, two potential pathways for producing material that could be used in nuclear weapons, Reuters reported.
